name: Mixed Neuroendocrine and Non-Neuroendocrine Neoplasm of Pancreas

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Digestive System (5th Edition)

criteria.description: Presence of both neuroendocrine and non-neuroendocrine malignant components confirmed by histopathological examination
Immunohistochemical staining positive for neuroendocrine markers (e.g., chromogranin A, synaptophysin) in neuroendocrine component
Each tumor component (neuroendocrine and non-neuroendocrine) constitutes at least 30% of the neoplasm

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of both neuroendocrine and non-neuroendocrine malignant components with immunohistochemical verification and each component comprising at least 30% of the tumor mass
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular studies may assist but are not mandatory for diagnosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pancreatic mass with mixed histological features
pathognomonic.notes: Identified on biopsy or surgical specimen
searchTerms: pancreatic tumor with mixed cell types

common.symptomName: Abdominal pain localized to the epigastrium

common.notes: May occur if tumor compresses bile duct
searchTerms: jaundice due to bile duct obstruction
skin and eye yellowing from liver issues

occasional.notes: Fatty stools from pancreatic enzyme deficiency

rare.symptomName: Hypoglycemia due to insulin secretion by neuroendocrine component
searchTerms: low blood sugar from insulin tumor
blood sugar drops due to tumor

laboratory: Elevated serum chromogranin A and neuron-specific enolase
Abnormal liver function tests if biliary obstruction present
Hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia depending on tumor secretory profile
imaging: Contrast-enhanced CT or MRI showing heterogeneous pancreatic mass
Somatostatin receptor scintigraphy (Octreoscan) or PET imaging for neuroendocrine component
Endoscopic ultrasound with fine needle aspiration biopsy
genetic: No specific germline mutations identified; sporadic cases predominate
Molecular profiling may reveal mutations common to pancreatic adenocarcinoma or neuroendocrine tumors
other: Histopathological examination demonstrating dual tumor components
Immunohistochemical staining positive for neuroendocrine markers and epithelial markers

distinguishingFeatures: Typically presents with ductal adenocarcinoma histology
Pure neuroendocrine tumor without non-neuroendocrine component

redFlags: Obstructive jaundice with worsening liver function
Severe hypoglycemia episodes in absence of diabetes
references: WHO Classification of Tumors Editorial Board. WHO Classification of Tumors: Digestive System Tumors. 5th ed. IARC; 2019.
La Rosa S, et al. Mixed neuroendocrine-non-neuroendocrine neoplasms (MiNENs): Unifying the concept of a heterogeneous group of neoplasms. Endocr Pathol. 2016;27(4):284-311.
Orphanet: Mixed neuroendocrine and non-neuroendocrine neoplasm of pancreas. ORPHA:506112.
